articles.title: Ketamine after the hype: What are we actually treating?
articles.abstract: ObjectiveKetamine has transformed depression research by demonstrating rapid antidepressant effects through mechanisms beyond monoaminergic neurotransmission. This perspective argues that the ketamine story also provides an opportunity to re-examine broader conceptual and methodological challenges in depression research, including the definition of treatment-resistant depression, patient selection, recruitment strategies, outcome measures and the interpretation of clinical trials.ConclusionsRather than questioning whether ketamine works, this perspective asks whether depression research generates evidence that meaningfully informs clinical decisions. Differences in patient populations, recruitment strategies, expectations and outcome measures may substantially shape treatment estimates. More precise clinical characterisation and greater emphasis on patient-important outcomes may help bridge the gap between efficacy demonstrated in trials and the choice of treatment for individual patients.

articles.title: Roots to Thrive risk and readiness assessment: a practice-based intake and decision-support framework for psychedelic-assisted therapy.
Baseline suicidal thoughts are associated with ECT non-remission and cognitive side effects: A network outcome analysis.
articles.abstract: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is effective for severe depression, yet remission is not universal and cognitive side effects remain a concern. Individual depressive symptoms may provide prognostic information beyond overall severity scores. In a multicentre cohort from the Dutch ECT Consortium, we applied network outcome analysis to seven symptoms harmonized across the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale and Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS). Outcomes were remission (N = 792) and in exploratory analysis, cognitive side effects (N = 100). Robustness was assessed through bootstrapping and sensitivity analyses, including established clinical predictors, an alternative remission definition, and multivariable logistic regression. Suicidal thoughts were associated with lower odds of remission (OR 0.77, bootstrapped confidence interval [bCI] 0.68-0.84) and higher odds of cognitive side effects (OR 1.34, bCI 1.15-2.02), with 98-100% and 72-91% bootstrap edge presence across sensitivity analyses, respectively. Reduced appetite was associated with higher remission odds (OR 1.08, bCI 1.03-1.22), with 70-94% bootstrap edge presence across sensitivity analyses, but the association was absent in the MADRS-specific analysis. Tension/anxiety was associated with higher odds of cognitive side effects (OR 1.26, bCI 1.14-1.92), with 77-84% bootstrap edge presence. After simultaneous covariate adjustment, logistic regression supported associations of suicidal thoughts with both outcomes and tension/anxiety with cognitive side effects; the adjusted cognitive model was exploratory. Baseline symptoms showed distinct associations with ECT outcomes. Suicidal thoughts were associated with both lower remission likelihood and higher odds of cognitive side effects, suggesting potential relevance for clinical monitoring and counselling.

articles.title: Mitochondrial respiratory chain activity in the brain of young male rats subjected to alloxan-induced diabetes and a ketamine-induced schizophrenia-like model.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1D) and schizophrenia (SZ) have both been associated with impaired brain energy metabolism. We investigated whether alloxan-induced insulin-deficient diabetes modifies the effects of a ketamine-induced schizophrenia-like model on the activity of brain mitochondrial respiratory chain enzymes. Male Wistar rats (23 days old) were assigned to four groups in a 2 × 2 factorial design: Control, Alloxan, Ketamine, and Ketamine + Alloxan. Diabetes was induced by a single intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of alloxan (150 mg/kg), and ketamine (25 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline was administered daily from day 4 to day 10. The activities of complexes I, II, II-III and IV were measured in tissue homogenates of the frontal cortex, hippocampus and striatum (n = 4 per group) and analyzed by two-way ANOVA, with correction for multiple testing across all outcomes. No observation was excluded from any analysis. Three effects remained significant after correction for multiple testing: alloxan was associated with lower complex II-III activity in the hippocampus (q = 0.016) and striatum (q = 0.016), and an alloxan × ketamine interaction was observed for complex I in the hippocampus (q = 0.016), where alloxan and ketamine each increased activity compared with controls whereas their combination did not. Before correction, ketamine was also associated with higher complex II activity in the hippocampus (p = 0.006) and interactions were detected for complex II-III (p = 0.046) and complex IV (p = 0.019) in the hippocampus and for complex I in the striatum (p = 0.031); these uncorrected findings should be regarded as exploratory. No significant effect of alloxan, ketamine or their interaction was detected for any enzyme in the frontal cortex. In this exploratory study, alloxan-induced diabetes and ketamine were associated with region- and enzyme-specific differences in respiratory chain enzyme activity in the hippocampus and striatum, with alloxan attenuating some ketamine-associated increases. These findings require replication in adequately powered studies including both sexes and complementary measures of mitochondrial function.

articles.title: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI in major depressive disorder: A systematic review of brain networks, neurovascular coupling, and clinical correlates.
articles.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging (EEG-fMRI) offers unique potential to characterize brain network dysfunction and neurovascular coupling in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the field lacks a rigorous synthesis restricted to strictly defined MDD populations with true multimodal integration. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261292902), we searched PubMed, Scopus, CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (inception to March 2026) for simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies in adults (≥18 years) with MDD. We excluded subclinical samples, healthy-only populations, and sequential acquisitions to ensure diagnostic specificity. Primary outcomes were network dysfunction, neurovascular coupling, and clinical associations. Narrative synthesis was performed due to data paucity (<3 studies/outcome). Risk of bias was assessed using modified ROB2, ROBINS-I, and JBI tools. Nine studies (eight cohorts; N=377) met strict criteria. Two reports from one cohort investigating anhedonia via neurofeedback (Zotev et al.) showed moderate-to-strong correlations between EEG-fMRI metrics and severity (r = 0.47 and 0.69). Single-study findings reported effect sizes for anxiety (r = 0.74), depression change (r = -0.38 to 0.90), and rumination (r = 0.20). Analytical heterogeneity was substantial. Evidence certainty was low due to bias risk and imprecision. Small sample sizes, methodological fragmentation, and reliance on single cohorts for specific outcomes limit generalizability. Simultaneous EEG-fMRI identifies strong neurophysiological correlates (e.g., anhedonia, treatment response) in active contexts (e.g., neurofeedback, ketamine), but evidence for generalizable resting-state biomarkers remains insufficient. Future efforts must prioritize standardized pipelines and large-scale cohorts to transition this technique to a clinical biomarker.

articles.title: Substance use to DSM-5 substance-specific and any substance use disorder in the U.S., 2021-2024.
articles.abstract: To estimate the number of U.S. individuals with Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) substance-specific substance use disorder (SUD) versus any DSM-5 SUD across 12 substances and assess SUD severity by polysubstance use. This cross-sectional study examined nationally representative data from the National Survey on Drug Use and Health collected annually in U.S. households from 2021 to 2024 among noninstitutionalized individuals aged ≥ 12 years (N = 232,441). Outcomes were DSM-5 substance-specific SUD, any SUD, and SUD severity estimates for individuals who reported past-year use of alcohol, cannabis, crack cocaine, other cocaine, hallucinogens, heroin, inhalants, methamphetamine, prescription opioids, sedatives, stimulants, and tranquilizers. Past-year substance-specific DSM-5 SUD prevalence ranged by substance used (5.2 % for prescription tranquilizers to 79.1 % for heroin). Most people who used substances other than alcohol or cannabis, or misused prescription medications met criteria for any SUD (59.7 % for inhalants to 92.1 % for heroin). Over 75 % of people reporting illicit stimulant use met criteria for any SUD. For past-year hallucinogen use, 5.3 % had a hallucinogen use disorder while 68.3 % had any SUD. Among people with SUD, mild severity was most common with 1-3 substances used (70.8 % for one; 52.7 % for three), while severe SUD was most prevalent among those using ≥ 5 substances (44.4 %). SUD prevalence was higher with polysubstance use versus single-substance use (34.3 % [≈37.2 million] versus 10.5 % [≈10.9 million]). DSM-5 SUD profiles vary across substances. Findings suggest the need for comprehensive assessment for DSM-5 SUD across all substances, especially with stimulant or polysubstance use.

articles.title: Domain-level symptom improvement after ketamine and TMS-based stimulation in treatment-resistant depression: a post hoc pooled analysis.
articles.abstract: We examined short-term symptom-domain improvement after ketamine and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in a post hoc pooled analysis of 159 active-treatment participants from three trials. Participants received a single ketamine infusion (n = 89) or a two-week TMS course (n = 70); nine had recorded bipolar diagnoses. Source trials used different treatment-resistance thresholds. We analyzed Depression, Anxiety, Insomnia, and Somatic indices derived from the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale. The primary analysis compared adjusted mean improvements across domains at day 14, with changes scaled by each domain's baseline standard deviation (SD). Models adjusted for baseline domain scores, age, and sex and used participant-cluster inference. Secondary analyses estimated baseline-adjusted correlations between continuous domain improvements. Mean improvement differed across domains within both modalities (both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Adjusted improvements for Depression, Anxiety, Insomnia, and Somatic were 1.48, 0.96, 0.46, and 0.45 SD units after ketamine and 1.71, 1.10, 0.72, and 0.78 after TMS. Main-model between-modality mean contrasts did not meet the adjusted threshold (p = 0.063-0.656); the Somatic contrast did so after adjustment for treatment-resistance categories. Direct correlation differences also did not meet the adjusted threshold (all p ≥ 0.085). These findings describe domain-specific improvement under different treatment regimens. Cross-modality comparisons remain exploratory and do not establish equivalence or guide treatment selection. UMIN000016985, UMIN000033916, UMIN000033760, and UMIN000020892.

articles.title: Oral Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy Leading to Prolonged Remission in Recurrent Dissociative Neurological Symptom Disorder With Mutism: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Dissociative neurological symptom disorder (DNSD), termed functional neurological symptom disorder in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, Text Revision (DSM-5-TR), presents with neurological symptoms not explained by structural disease. The first line treatment of DNSD is psychotherapy, but when the conflict maintaining the symptoms cannot be put into words, psychotherapy often stalls. This report describes a 56-year-old woman with a four-year history of episodic loss of consciousness and progressive speech loss, with normal neurological investigations. Escitalopram, intravenous ketamine infusions given without psychotherapy, and venlafaxine produced no meaningful benefit. A 30-day inpatient program of psychotherapy, family therapy, and speech therapy restored her speech, but she relapsed into complete mutism four months after discharge, and no stressor could be identified. A lorazepam-assisted interview produced sedation without speech. She then received six alternate-day sessions of oral ketamine-assisted psychotherapy, titrated from 50 mg to 150 mg, within a psychodynamically informed frame; while venlafaxine 225 mg/day was continued and family therapy was delivered alongside. She spoke a few words in the third session (100 mg) and conversed spontaneously in the fourth (150 mg), describing a conflict between a rigid moral self-image of never being greedy and unspoken distress over a family property dispute. Speech has been sustained for more than one year, and all psychotropic medication has since been withdrawn. The report proposes that, this single case is hypothesis-generating. It suggests that ketamine may be a useful and a better abreactive agent in selected patients with treatment-resistant DNSD, and that the therapeutic frame is also essential for the improvement to happen, and further controlled comparison with benzodiazepine-assisted interviews is warranted in the future.

articles.title: A multiple Arc tagging approach for tracking neuronal ensembles across experiences.
articles.abstract: Engrams, or memory traces, are the neuronal ensembles that collectively store individual experiences. Genetic strategies based on immediate early genes (IEGs), such as Arc/Arg3.1, allow for the ensembles active during memory encoding to be tagged and compared to those active during retrieval. However, these strategies only allow for the tagging of one neural ensemble. Here, we developed a multiple Arc (mArc) system that allows for the tagging of two Arc

articles.title: PROPOFOL VERSUS WITH PROPOFOL-KETAMINE MIXTURE AS ANAESTHETIC AGENT FOR ELECTROCONVULSIVE THERAPY: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL.
articles.abstract: Ketamine either alone or as an adjuvant is associated with an acute reduction in the severity of depression, while its effect on cognitive profile is is equivocal. This study compared the mood-elevating and cognitive outcomes of ketamine in combination with propofol versus propofol alone as anaesthetic agents in ECT. In this randomised-controlled study, 70 patients, aged 18-65years, undergoing ECT for DSM-V major depressive disorder were randomised into two groups. The ketamine-propofol group received intravenous propofol 0.6mg/kg and ketamine 0.6mg/kg, while the second group received intravenous propofol 1.2mg/kg only. Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) was used to assess the severity of depression, the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) was used to assess cognitive performance, pre-ECT (T1), post-1st ECT (T2) and post-3rd ECT course (T3). The Analysis of Covariance and the mixed model linear regression were used to analyse the effect of the intervention. Analyses were by SPSS at 95% CI, p < 0.05. There was a significant reduction in HAM-D score post-3rd ECT in the ketamine-propofol group versus propofol group, F (1,58) = 23.24, p = 0.000, h = 0.286. There was no significant group difference on post-ECT course HAM-D score, F (1) = 0.004, p = 0.9. There was no significant group difference on post-ECT course MMSE scores, F (1) = 2.3, p = 0.1. There was no significant group difference on post-3rd ECT MMSE score, F (1,56) = 0.382, P = 0.5, 5?2 = 0.007, no significant group difference on post-ECT course MMSE scores, (F(1) = 2.3, p = 0.1. Ketamine-propofol anaesthesia in ECT is associated with temporary improvement of depressive symptoms, without any superiority to propofol in cognitive outcome at any level of ECT treatment.

articles.title: Connectedness as a candidate pathway linking psilocybin retreat experiences to sustained wellbeing: a prospective naturalistic study.
articles.abstract: Psychedelic retreats are increasingly used to promote wellbeing outside clinical settings, yet the psychological processes associated with sustained improvements in wellbeing remain poorly understood. From a public mental health perspective, identifying mechanisms that support positive mental health beyond symptom reduction is of growing importance. This naturalistic longitudinal study followed 173 participants attending guided psilocybin retreats conducted within a structured framework of preparation, dosing, and integration. Mental wellbeing was reported before the retreat and across a 12-month follow-up period. Longitudinal changes were examined using linear mixed-effects models. Mediation analyses investigated whether changes in connectedness, neuroticism (anxiety facet), spiritual transcendence, and absorption were associated with changes in wellbeing. Mystical-type experiences were examined as potential predictors of these psychological changes. Participants reported substantial and sustained improvements in mental wellbeing over 12 months, moving from levels below Swedish population norms at baseline toward comparable levels at follow-up. Connectedness showed the strongest statistical association with improvements in wellbeing and accounted for the largest proportion of variance in wellbeing change, followed by reductions in the anxiety facet of neuroticism and absorption. Spiritual transcendence was associated with wellbeing improvements when examined separately but did not retain unique effects in the multiple mediation model. More intense mystical-type experiences predicted greater increases in connectedness, spirituality, and absorption, as well as greater reductions in neuroticism (trait anxiety). The association between mystical experiences and wellbeing was substantially attenuated when connectedness was included in the model, suggesting that connectedness may act as a candidate mediator linking mystical-type experiences to longer-term wellbeing, though the observational design precludes causal inference. These findings extend prior work on psychedelic-assisted therapy to naturalistic retreat settings, suggesting that connectedness may represent a key psychological process linking psychedelic retreat experiences to sustained improvements in mental wellbeing. From a public mental health perspective, the results highlight the potential importance of social and relational factors in promoting wellbeing beyond the treatment of mental illness. Future controlled studies are needed to clarify the relative contributions of psychedelic, social, and contextual components.

articles.title: From Rapid Synaptic Events to Lasting Antidepressant States: Convergent and Divergent Mechanisms of Ketamine and Psychedelics.
articles.abstract: Rapid-acting antidepressants have challenged the long-standing view that therapeutic improvement in major depressive disorder requires chronic treatment with monoaminergic agents. Ketamine and classical psychedelics act through distinct proximal targets, yet both can produce rapid and persistent behavioral effects that implicate synaptic and circuit plasticity as the core mechanisms of antidepressant action. This review, based on a minisymposium presented at the 2026 Society for Neuroscience meeting, examines how brief pharmacological perturbations translate into lasting changes in mood-related networks. We first discuss hippocampal mechanisms underlying ketamine action, which include brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)/tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB)-dependent homeostatic potentiation, TrkB cross talk with metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) at CA3→CA1 synapses, extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK)-dual-specificity phosphatase 6 (DUSP6)-mediated extension of synaptic metaplasticity, and BDNF release at mossy fiber synapses and dentate gyrus neuronal maturation. We then consider how these local plasticity mechanisms interface with distributed circuits that regulate motivation, stress coping, and reward. Across brain regions, emerging work highlights the importance of cell type- and region-specific mechanisms that mediate ketamine's therapeutic actions. We expand on local prefrontal cortical inhibitory cellular signaling dynamics, including the interplay of various G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) in cortical somatostatin interneurons and input-specific adaptations in accumbal circuits. Finally, we compare ketamine with psilocybin, an emerging therapeutic classic psychedelic for treatment-resistant depression that targets the 5-hydroxytryptamine 2A (5-HT2A) receptor primarily. A recurring theme is that an interplay of GPCRs can help shape the timing, localization, and persistence of ketamine-induced neuroplasticity. Together, these studies suggest that antidepressant efficacy arises not from a single pathway or brain region but from coordinated, temporally staged plasticity across molecules, synapses, cells, and circuits.

articles.title: Parallel Claustral Networks for Behavioral Control in Health and Disease.
articles.abstract: The claustrum is among the most highly interconnected structures in the mammalian brain, with reciprocal projections spanning the cortical mantle and a growing roster of functions that range from sleep regulation to attentional control. Here we review current understanding of claustral circuit organization and function, synthesizing findings from anatomical, physiological, computational, and behavioral studies. We argue that a unifying logic underlies the apparent diversity of claustral functions: the claustrum operates through projection-defined subnetworks whose input selectivity, output targets, and local circuit interactions collectively determine their functional contribution and whose impact on cortical targets varies with arousal and ongoing brain state. Corticoclaustral connectivity is organized into matched input-output modules, local inhibitory circuits confer spatial filtering properties that amplify strong cortical signals while suppressing weaker ones and claustral output populations differ in their laminar targets, postsynaptic cell-type preferences, and molecular properties, producing diverse and context-dependent effects on cortical dynamics. These circuit properties translate into claustral regulation of cortical population dynamics across multiple timescales, from the moment-to-moment coordination of brain states to the consolidation of frontal control strategies. In pain and addiction, specific claustral projection populations are selectively dysregulated, and distinct subnetworks exert opposing influences on nociceptive sensitivity and drug-related behavior according to their cortical targets. Together, these findings position the claustrum as a modular subcortical hub for the selective regulation of distributed cortical networks and identify it as a candidate therapeutic target for disorders characterized by dysregulated cortical network activity, including chronic pain, addiction, and impulsivity.

articles.title: Fifty years at the addiction bench and bedside: from withdrawal syndromes to adaptive brain states.
articles.abstract: Over the past half-century, addiction medicine has moved from moral and symptom-based explanations toward a neuroscience of adaptation, learning, motivation, and recovery. This Perspective uses several linked translational programs-opioid withdrawal and the locus coeruleus, cocaine dependence and dopamine, environmental drug exposure, physician health, and food reward-to illustrate how observations at the bedside can generate mechanistic studies and how laboratory findings can, in turn, change treatment and public health. LC stimulation produced signs and symptoms that looked to me like opioid withdrawal. So, we thought that noradrenergic hyperactivity in opioid withdrawal caused symptoms, and while methadone or morphine could treat these, we could also treat them with a non-opioid, clonidine. Earlier noradrenergic interventions had been attempted with limited clinical success. Our work provided the first hypothesis-driven, double-blind, placebo-controlled demonstration that a non-opioid medication could suppress the acute human opioid withdrawal syndrome. This mechanism-based treatment was greeted with considerable interest because some clinicians had assumed that any medication capable of reversing opioid withdrawal distress must itself be an opioid. Clonidine and later lofexidine did just that and facilitated transition to naltrexone. Recognition that cocaine could produce compulsive use without a dramatic physical withdrawal syndrome helped shift the field toward reward circuitry, craving, pathological attraction, anhedonia, and relapse. Studies of tobacco, cannabis, and opioid smoke broadened prevention by showing that involuntary second- and third-hand exposure can be biologically detected and, most clearly for tobacco, can produce biologically meaningful effects. Third-hand exposure refers to residual drug-related contaminants that persist on indoor surfaces, dust, clothing, or other materials after active smoking has ended. Contemporary work on neuromodulation, exercise, psychedelics, and GLP-1 metabolic-reward pathways extends the same translational logic. Addiction is best understood as an acquired adaptive brain state supported by anti-survival or bad learning, development, and environment; recovery is active neurobehavioral relearning, not simply detoxification or drug clearance. Public health should therefore join brain sciences, work to delay initiation, identify emerging risk before a severe substance use disorder develops, prevent involuntary exposure, and provide rapid access to mechanism-based treatment, recovery-supportive environments, and outcomes measured over 5 years or longer.

articles.title: Psychedelic ego-dissolution: a philosophical and qualitative critique.
articles.abstract: Ego-dissolution is a phenomenon of central interest across interdisciplinary research on psychedelics. In this paper, we present a philosophical and qualitative critique of the claim that ego-dissolution can result in conscious states with no phenomenal sense of self, i.e., states that completely lack any form of self-consciousness. We first turn to recent publications by Chris Letheby and Raphaël Millière, for whom trip reports of experiences induced by 5-MeO-DMT (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine) present clear evidence for the existence of totally selfless experiential states. Their claim is undermined, we argue, by the fact that they operate with overinflated notions of 'self' and 'self-consciousness,' meaning that more minimal forms are available and arguably still present in 5-MeO-DMT experiences. We then perform a qualitative thematic analysis of 411 5-MeO-DMT trip reports. Pointing to the ambiguous language of the trip reports, the self-admitted inadequacy of the descriptions and the affective dimension of the reported experiences, we argue that claims concerning total selflessness are unwarranted and instead offer an alternative interpretation: extreme ego-dissolution during 5-MeO-DMT experiences involves a radically minimal form of self-consciousness, one in which the identity of the subject is experienced as unfamiliar and underdetermined. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.

articles.title: Changes in self-related cognitive processes and depressive symptom severity following a single, moderate dose of psilocybin in depressed patients.
articles.abstract: Psychedelic-assisted therapy, particularly with psilocybin, is increasingly proposed as a treatment for major depressive disorder, yet the neural and psychological mechanisms underlying its effects remain under investigation. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, individuals diagnosed with major depressive disorder received a single, moderate dose of psilocybin (0.215 mg kg-1) or placebo, with the same psychological support. We analysed N = 37 individuals with major depressive disorder undergoing assessments of depressive symptoms (Beck's depression inventory and Montgomery-Åsberg depression rating scale), self-concept (Frankfurt self-concept scale) and neural markers of self-referential processing using an fMRI-based task. Compared with placebo, the psilocybin group exhibited significant reductions in depressive symptoms and a significant increase in positive self-concept two weeks after substance administration. Changes in self-concept were significantly correlated with decreased depressive scores. Neuroimaging revealed psilocybin-associated modulation of caudate activation during externally oriented attention after two weeks, contrasting with placebo-induced caudate changes during self-referential processing. These findings extend prior evidence linking psychedelics to changes in self-referential processing and self-concept and demonstrate that such changes occur concurrently with reductions in depressive symptoms. Future research should aim to replicate and extend these results and refine therapy protocols targeting self-processing and self-concept in psychedelic-assisted therapy in major depressive disorder. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.

articles.title: Is ibogaine treatment durable? 12-month follow-up of magnesium-ibogaine therapy (MISTIC) in special operations veterans with traumatic brain injuries.
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) can result in chronic functional disability and is associated with persistent psychiatric symptoms, including posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, and anxiety. Ibogaine, an oneirogenic alkaloid with unique pharmacological properties, has shown initial promise as a potential treatment for TBI-related sequelae. We previously observed large improvements in functional and psychiatric outcomes up to one month after a single treatment with magnesium-ibogaine in male U.S. Special Operations Veterans with a history of TBI. However, further evidence on the durability of these effects is needed. In this prospective long-term follow-up study, we evaluated the persistence of these clinical improvements over the subsequent year. Participants underwent comprehensive baseline and post-treatment assessments, with follow-up evaluations conducted at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. Of 30 participants treated with magnesium-ibogaine, 25 completed the 12-month follow-up assessments. Outcome measures included a self-report measure of functional disability and clinician-administered assessments of psychiatric symptoms. Linear mixed-effects models demonstrated robust and sustained reductions in disability, PTSD, depression, and anxiety symptoms through 12 months post-treatment (all p < 0.001 after correction for multiple comparisons), with large effect sizes (Cohen's d ≥ 2.18 at 12 months). In participants who achieved remission immediately post-treatment, survival analyses estimated the probability of sustained remission at 12 months as 84% for PTSD, 66% for depression, and 61% for anxiety. Notably, most participants reported using other psychedelic substances or pursuing other interventions during the follow-up period, which should be considered when interpreting long-term symptom trajectories. In this naturalistic cohort, durable, clinically meaningful symptom improvements were observed in individuals with TBI up to 12 months after ibogaine treatment. Further investigation through randomized controlled trials is warranted to validate these promising preliminary results and clarify the causal contributions of ibogaine treatment, subsequent interventions, and their combination.

articles.title: Ketamine for co-occurring chronic pain and depression: A scoping review highlighting the dual-outcome evidence gap and its treatment and research implications.
articles.abstract: Chronic pain and depression frequently co-occur, share clinical features, and involve shared neurobiological substrates. Ketamine, an NMDA-receptor antagonist, has established antidepressant efficacy, whereas its analgesic efficacy for chronic pain remains uncertain. Given the overlap between chronic pain and depression, ketamine may serve as a potential dual-action treatment. We conducted a scoping review of studies in which pain and depressive outcomes were both assessed longitudinally after ketamine treatment. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus through August 2026. Experimental and observational studies reporting post-treatment pain and depression outcomes were included; acute, perioperative, perinatal, and cancer-related pain were excluded. Of 2187 records screened, 12 studies met inclusion criteria (2007-2025). Eight enrolled patients with consensus-based chronic pain (≥3 months); among these, only two used clinical diagnoses to characterize depression (one being retrospective chart review), whereas the remainder used symptom scales. Four depression-primary studies enrolled patients with major depressive disorder, treatment-resistant depression, or bipolar depression but did not rigorously establish chronic pain duration. Most studies reported concurrent improvement in pain and depressive symptoms, but heterogeneity in population definitions, ketamine administration regimens, study design, and psychiatric comorbidity precludes inference that depression modifies ketamine's analgesic effect. Prospective randomized studies using standardized chronic pain and depression measures are needed to clarify ketamine's efficacy and real-world applicability. REGISTRATION: This protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF) (registration: OSF.IO/3ER5W) PERSPECTIVE: This review maps studies that assessed pain and depressive symptoms longitudinally during ketamine treatment. Concurrent improvement was commonly reported, but inconsistent depression ascertainment, pain phenotyping, dosing, and study design prevent conclusions about depression-specific analgesic effects. Prospective trials with clinically defined comorbidity are needed.

articles.title: Current perspectives in the pharmacological treatment of gambling disorder: psychedelics and beyond.
articles.abstract: Gambling disorder (GD) is a heterogeneous behavioral addiction associated with dysregulated reward processing, impaired executive control, stress-system dysfunction, and maladaptive neuroplasticity. Despite its considerable clinical, social, and economic burden, no medication is currently approved specifically for GD, and available pharmacological strategies remain off label. This narrative review examines established and emerging pharmacological approaches to GD. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language literature published between January 2010 and January 2026. Opioid antagonists show the most consistent, although still limited, therapeutic signal with potential benefits in selected patients with prominent gambling urges, whereas evidence for antidepressants, mood stabilizers, antiepileptic drugs, and antipsychotics remains heterogeneous. Glutamatergic, noradrenergic, endocannabinoid, and orexin-related interventions are biologically plausible but largely experimental. Psychedelic and neuroplasticity-oriented treatments, including psilocybin, ketamine/esketamine, and 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA)-assisted interventions, may target cognitive inflexibility, compulsive behavior, and maladaptive reward learning. The available evidence supports a cautious, mechanism-informed approach to pharmacological research, while underscoring the need for adequately powered clinical trials and prospective evaluation of clinically relevant treatment-response indicators. Pharmacotherapy for GD should move toward phenotype-informed, multimodal treatment rather than a one-size-fits-all model. Emerging neuroplasticity-based interventions are promising, but adequately powered, controlled, and longitudinal trials are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Adapted Massed Exposure Therapy Enhanced with MDMA for PTSD (aMETEMP): A randomized, double-masked protocol adapted for Veterans Affairs healthcare system.
articles.abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) remains prevalent and disabling, especially among veterans, with a substantial proportion failing to achieve remission following first-line evidence-based trauma-focused psychotherapies. 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) is hypothesized to enhance psychotherapy outcomes through effects on fear extinction, cognitive flexibility, and emotional engagement, and is being studied as a promising augmentation strategy for PTSD psychotherapy. There is limited research combining MDMA with evidence-based PTSD treatment. MDMA-assisted psychotherapy trials to date have also been limited by lack of an active comparator and functional unmasking. We describe the methodology of an ongoing randomized, double-masked, pilot trial evaluating massed prolonged exposure (PE) therapy enhanced with MDMA for PTSD (aMETEMP), adapted for a U.S. Veterans Affairs outpatient setting. Up to 20 veterans with PTSD in the VA will receive a 6-8hr in-person MDMA dosing session (randomized dose 35 mg - 125 mg) integrated with a 3-week massed exposure protocol. The remaining visits are virtual and include PE sessions and sessions to prepare for and process the MDMA session (28-30hrs total over 11 visits), with the use of telehealth intended to improve access and ease patient burden. After treating the first 4 participants, who were fully informed of the trial design, we switched to using an incomplete disclosure strategy (not disclosing the number of treatment arms or specific possible doses) to further improve masking. Primary outcomes include PTSD severity using the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5, safety, feasibility, and masking success. Findings are intended to provide preliminary descriptive information regarding feasibility, safety/tolerability, masking integrity, and symptom-change signals for aMETEMP with incomplete disclosure in a large outpatient healthcare system. NCT06117306.

articles.title: Breaking: Helus’ Deuterated Psilocin Hits Primary Endpoint in First Phase 3

articles.title: A let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicle-laden bioactive scaffold promotes immunomodulation and regeneration of segmental tracheal defects.
articles.abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. Persistent post-injury inflammation, inadequate neovascularization, and delayed epithelial restoration contribute to the formation of granulation tissue and subsequent graft failure. In this study, we developed a bioactive tracheal scaffold for sustained local delivery of let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicles (let-7a-5p-EVs) to modulate the regenerative microenvironment during tracheal repair. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In a rabbit segmental tracheal defect model, the let-7a-5p-EV-laden scaffold enhanced neovascularization, mitigated local inflammatory responses, promoted mucociliary epithelial reconstruction, and maintained airway patency. The let-7a-5p-EV scaffold improved biomechanical recovery, and increased survival rates. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation indicated that these effects were associated with the attenuation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-associated inflammatory activation, as evidenced by reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. These findings demonstrate that sustained local delivery of engineered EVs from a mechanically competent bioactive scaffold provides an effective immunomodulatory strategy for the regenerative repair of segmental tracheal defects and offers translational potential for functional airway reconstruction.

articles.title: Update on Sedation for Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy in Japan: Current Evidence on Remimazolam.
articles.abstract: Sedation is an essential component of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy because it reduces patient discomfort and anxiety while improving patient acceptance and procedural quality. In Japan, benzodiazepines such as midazolam and opioid analgesics have long been widely used in routine clinical practice; however, many of these agents historically lacked formal insurance approval for sedation during gastrointestinal endoscopy. Propofol is also a useful sedative because of its rapid onset and recovery, but its use in Japan has been limited because of concerns regarding respiratory and cardiovascular depression and the need for management by anesthesia-trained personnel. Against this background, the approval of remimazolam for sedation during gastrointestinal endoscopy in June 2025 represented a major turning point in Japanese endoscopic sedation practice. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine rapidly metabolized by carboxylesterases and reversible with flumazenil. Japanese phase III trials demonstrated high sedation success rates and rapid recovery during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, including in elderly patients. Compared with midazolam, remimazolam shortened awakening and ambulation times, whereas compared with propofol, it may cause fewer respiratory and cardiovascular adverse events. This review summarizes the current status of upper gastrointestinal endoscopic sedation in Japan, focusing on the clinical evidence and positioning of the newly approved ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, remimazolam.

articles.title: Pain Management in the Trauma Patient.
articles.abstract: Effective pain management in adult trauma patients is essential to improve recovery, reduce complications, and prevent long-term consequences such as chronic pain, depression, and PTSD. Multimodal analgesia combines medications and nonpharmacologic strategies to achieve better pain control while minimizing opioid use and associated risks. Key agents include acetaminophen, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents, ketamine, topical and systemic lidocaine, gabapentinoids, muscle relaxants, and carefully selected opioids when necessary. Pain management should be individualized based on patient factors, including age, comorbidities, traumatic brain injury, and substance use disorders. Early assessment, regular reassessment, and coordinated multidisciplinary care optimize outcomes across trauma settings.

articles.title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
articles.abstract:
Purpose

Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair.

Methods

Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA.

Results

We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+).

Conclusions

Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

articles.title: Glis1 regulates metabolic programming by promoting H3K18 lactylation to alleviate neuronal senescence following spinal cord injury.
articles.abstract: Neuronal senescence is a significant factor impeding spinal cord injury (SCI) repair. Research indicates that Glis1, a Kruppel-like zinc finger transcription factor, is pivotal in reprogramming senescent cells and enhancing genomic stability via lactylation. Histone lactylation, an epigenetic modification using lactate as a substrate, becomes prominent post-SCI due to increased neuronal lactate levels. However, the mechanisms linking neuronal senescence and histone lactylation following SCI remain poorly understood. This study elucidates the roles of Glis1, H3K18 lactylation, and neuronal senescence through comprehensive in vivo and in vitro investigations. The findings reveal a post-SCI rise in neuronal lactate levels, accompanied by cellular senescence. Furthermore, upregulation of Glis1 attenuates senescence and promotes histone lactylation. The downstream target secretogranin II (SCG2), identified via ChIP-seq and RNA-seq, was found to exert negative feedback on glycolytic metabolism and lactylation, thereby suppressing neuronal senescence. These results unveil a novel regulatory mechanism of Glis1 in neuronal senescence following SCI through the p300/H3K18la/SCG2 axis, offering a new therapeutic target for spinal cord repair.

articles.title: A bioactivity-enhanced thermosensitive amnion-derived hydrogel with sustained IGF-1 release: A multitargeted and efficient strategy for corneal injury repair.
articles.abstract: Corneal alkali burn (CAB) remains difficult to treat because rapid tear clearance limits topical drug exposure, while the injured cornea develops a complex microenvironment involving inflammation, neovascularization, fibrosis, epithelial barrier loss, and impaired nerve repair. Here, we developed a human amniotic membrane-derived thermosensitive hydrogel (hAMgel) and loaded it with insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) to create a bioactive sustained-release system (IGF1@hAMgel) for CAB repair. The hAMgel transformed from a flowable precursor into a semi-transparent film on the ocular surface within 1-2 min and IGF1@hAMgel released approximately 90% of loaded IGF-1 over 24 h, with corneal IGF-1 concentration peaking at 2 h post-dose (378.5 pg/mg protein) and remaining detectable over 24 h, supporting sustained topical exposure. In a rat CAB model, IGF1@hAMgel accelerated epithelial healing, reducing the fluorescein-stained area from 31.34 ± 2.83% in controls to 16.78 ± 2.87% at day 1. By day 14, IGF1@hAMgel reduced corneal opacity (0.67 ± 0.52 vs. 4.00 ± 0.00), resolved edema with central corneal thickness approaching baseline (187.7 ± 16.31 μm vs. 178.3 ± 5.89 μm), suppressed neovascularization (CD31-positive area 4.46 ± 1.69% vs. 24.33 ± 2.07%), and promoted corneal nerve regeneration. Proteomic analysis showed that hAMgel retained abundant extracellular matrix(ECM) components, including collagens, Lumican, and fibronectin, together with repair-related and immunomodulatory proteins. These findings identify IGF1@hAMgel as a sutureless, eye-drop-like bioactive ECM platform that integrates growth-factor delivery with amnion-derived reparative cues for multitargeted ocular surface repair.

articles.title: A self-crosslinkable, adhesive intestine-derived extracellular matrix hydrogel enhances organoid retention and restores intestinal barrier integrity.
articles.abstract: Disruption of the intestinal barrier impairs essential functions of the gastrointestinal tract and triggers severe inflammation. Accordingly, transplantation of intestinal organoids restores the integrity of the injured intestinal barrier by promoting regeneration. However, the dynamic mucosal microenvironment of the intestine hinders effective retention of transplanted organoids, thereby limiting their therapeutic efficacy. To address this challenge, this study introduces a pyrogallol (PG)-conjugated intestine-derived extracellular matrix (IEM) (IEM-PG) as a scaffold for effective organoid transplantation. The dual crosslinking of IEM-based fibrillogenesis and oxidative PG coupling enabled IEM-PG to form a robust hydrogel scaffold without crosslinking agents under physiological conditions. Moreover, the IEM-PG hydrogel exhibited enhanced mechanical properties, superior bio-adhesion, and greater resistance to enzymatic degradation than the pristine IEM. The IEM-PG hydrogel was also highly biocompatible and did not adversely affect the viability and development of colonic organoids. The solution-type IEM-PG was readily injected into colonic tissue, thus allowing IEM-PG to initially spread along the intestinal lining. Transplantation of colonic organoids using IEM-PG in a mouse colonic ulcer model demonstrated effective cell retention in the intestinal tract, thereby restoring the structural integrity and function of the intestinal barrier. The study further demonstrated that the patch-type IEM-PG hydrogel was effective for the transplantation of colonic assembloids and the treatment of colonic perforation. Overall, this study presents the IEM engineered with an adhesive motif as a self-crosslinking hydrogel platform for organoid/assembloid transplantation and intestinal tissue repair.

articles.title: Rapid antidepressant-like effects of Chaihu Shugan San in female restraint-stressed mice: involvement of hippocampal TC2N and ERβ-eNOS-CaMKII-BDNF signaling.
articles.abstract:
Ethnopharmacological relevance

Chaihu Shugan San (CSS), a classical seven-herb formula from the Ming-dynasty text Jing-Yue Quanshu, is widely prescribed for depressive disorders in China. Previous preclinical studies reported antidepressant-like effects only after weeks of repeated administration, mostly in male animals. Whether a single dose of CSS can produce rapid antidepressant-like effects in female animals, and through what mechanism, remains unclear.

Aim of the study

To determine whether a single administration of CSS produces rapid antidepressant-like effects in female mice exposed to chronic restraint stress (CRS), and to explore the underlying hippocampal mechanism.

Methods and materials

CSS quality was controlled by HPLC quantification of four index components. Female CRS mice received a single dose of CSS (1, 2 or 4 g/kg, i. g.) or ketamine (10 mg/kg, i. p.), followed by behavioral testing (tail suspension, forced swimming, sucrose preference and open field tests) within 2-24 h. Hippocampal RNA sequencing, RT-qPCR, Western blotting and ELISA were used to identify and validate candidate targets; hippocampal AAV-mediated TC2N overexpression and pretreatment with the ERβ antagonist acolbifene or the CaMKII inhibitor KN-93 were used for interventional validation.

Results

Batch-to-batch variation of the four index components was below 10% (RSDs 3.51-5.66%), with naringin (313.07 ± 11.16 μg/mL) and hesperidin (196.40 ± 11.11 μg/mL) as the major constituents. Acute administration of CSS (2 and 4 g/kg), like ketamine, shortened immobility time in the tail suspension test at 2 h and in the forced swimming test at 12 h, and restored sucrose preference at 24 h, without affecting locomotor activity. Hippocampal transcriptomics identified Tc2n as up-regulated by CRS and down-regulated by CSS, with Esr2, Nos3 and Camk2a showing the opposite pattern; these changes were confirmed at the mRNA and protein levels within 2 h. Hippocampal TC2N overexpression or pretreatment with acolbifene or KN-93 abolished the rapid behavioral effects of CSS and the associated changes in ERβ-eNOS-CaMKII-BDNF signaling.

Conclusion

CSS produces rapid, ketamine-comparable antidepressant-like behavioral effects in female CRS-exposed mice, accompanied by down-regulation of hippocampal TC2N and involvement of ERβ, eNOS, CaMKII and BDNF. Because only female mice were studied, these findings are specific to females and support an estrogen-linked mechanism that warrants confirmation in male animals and further translational study.

articles.title: Barcoded oligonucleotide system (BOLT) for targeted organ delivery.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic potential of oligonucleotides (oligos) is limited by insufficient delivery to extrahepatic tissues. In vitro assays often fail to accurately predict in vivo behavior, while testing each oligo candidate in animals remains inherently low throughput. Here, we conceive a barcoded oligonucleotide system (BOLT), a platform that enables high-throughput in vivo evaluations of small-molecule ligands and identifies tissue-specific oligo delivery. BOLT integrates rational design of oligo barcodes, modular conjugation chemistry, and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based quantification, allowing simultaneous evaluation of many chemically diverse ligand-oligo conjugates within a single animal. Notably, this platform is applicable in both mice and nonhuman primates (NHPs). Using BOLT, we discovered ligands with tropism for tissues such as the brain, lung, and muscle. Collectively, these results indicate that the BOLT platform can accelerate the discovery of tissue-targeting ligands for broad oligo therapeutics.

articles.title: Ultrasound-activated piezoelectric muscle constructs for tissue-engineered regenerative peripheral nerve interfaces.
articles.abstract: Regenerative peripheral nerve interfaces (RPNIs) are emerging platforms capable to translate neural activity into controllable myoelectric signals. However, current clinical RPNIs rely on muscle autografts, limiting their scalability and extensive adoption. Here, we report a bioactive, ultrasound-responsive piezoelectric muscle biomaterial designed as a fully tissue-engineered alternative to autologous grafts. The construct consists of fibrinogen-based muscle tissues enriched with barium titanate nanoparticles (BTNPs, diameter∼60 nm) and supported by a biodegradable surgical membrane that promotes the formation of aligned, multinucleated myotubes. The incorporation of BTNPs imparts intrinsic piezoelectric activity to the construct, and the nanoparticles are taken up by developing myotubes, enabling remote mechanoelectrical tissue stimulation under low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS). In vivo, piezoelectric constructs implanted around the rat peroneal nerve for two months undergo LIPUS-driven activation of internalized BTNPs, which enhances muscle maturation, and electromechanical responsiveness, yielding myoelectrical signals up to 3.2 mV upon nerve activation. Histological analyses confirm improved structural organization, increased desmin expression, and evidence of neovascularization and axonal regeneration within the engineered interface. These findings suggest that the piezoelectric constructs form stable, functional biointerfaces with peripheral nerves, and that LIPUS-driven activation of embedded BTNPs provides a non-invasive strategy to potentiate muscle development and signal transduction. This study positions LIPUS-responsive, engineered piezoelectric muscle constructs as a donor-free, bioactive platform alternative to traditional autografts for next-generation human-machine interfaces and regenerative bioelectronics.

Subacute and long-term changes in cognitive functioning after administration of classic psychedelics, MDMA and ketamine: A systematic review of clinical and preclinical evidence
articles.abstract: Psychedelic agents induce a window of heightened neuroplasticity that extends beyond acute intoxication, during which neural circuits are more amenable to change. This period may facilitate changes in cognition relevant to the treatment of psychiatric disorders. This systematic review synthesised clinical and preclinical evidence of subacute and long-term (≥1 day) effects of classic and non-classic psychedelics on cognition. MEDLINE, EMBASE, APA PsycInfo and Web of Science were searched to identify human and animal studies investigating psychedelics and cognition (executive function, attention, decision-making). Sixty-seven (47 clinical, 20 preclinical) articles met inclusion criteria. Psilocybin demonstrated the most consistent evidence of subacute and longer-term cognitive improvement, particularly in cognitive flexibility and attention. Ketamine showed enhancement across cognitive domains, although findings were heterogeneous. LSD and DMT showed no consistent subacute changes, while MDMA was associated with transient cognitive impairments that resolved within days. Risk of bias assessments revealed selective outcome reporting, poor reporting of missing data and inadequate methodological detail, limiting the confidence of findings. Current evidence provides preliminary support for subacute changes in cognition following administration of select psychedelic agents. Cognitive improvements were more frequently seen in psychiatric populations than healthy subjects, which may re

articles.title: Psychedelics and autism spectrum disorder: Mechanistic insights, translational evidence and ethical challenges
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and interaction, restricted and repetitive patterns of behavior, and sensory processing alterations, frequently accompanied by anxiety, emotional dysregulation, and other psychiatric comorbidities. Despite advances in behavioral and pharmacological interventions, effective treatments for core ASD symptoms remain limited. Psychedelic compounds have recently emerged as potential therapeutic agents in psychiatry because of their ability to modulate serotonergic and glutamatergic signaling, enhance neuroplasticity, reorganize large-scale brain networks, and influence neurobiological pathways implicated in ASD. In this narrative review, we examine the mechanistic rationale supporting psychedelic-based approaches in ASD, including 5-HT2A receptor activation, oxytocin-serotonin interactions, excitation-inhibition dynamics, functional connectivity, and glutamatergic modulation associated with ketamine and related compounds. We also summarize current clinical and preclinical evidence involving substances such as psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide, 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine, and ketamine. Particular attention is given to the distinction between core ASD symptoms and associated symptom domains. articles.title: Prevalence and Reasons for Microdosing Cannabis, Psilocybin, LSD, and MDMA Among U.S. Adults
articles.abstract: Microdosing involves consuming low doses of psychoactive substances, typically 1/5th to 1/20th of a recreational dose. Despite increasing public attention to cannabis and psychedelics amid evolving drug policies, epidemiological data on microdosing remain limited.A cross-sectional, web-based survey (Characterizing the Epidemiology of Cannabidiol Use Survey) of 1,525 US adults was conducted in October-November 2023 and analyzed in 2024-2025 using Ipsos KnowledgePanel. Participants reported lifetime microdosing of cannabis, psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), and 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA). Lifetime prevalence, frequency, and reasons for microdosing were assessed, along with associations with demographics, mental health, quality of life, and cannabis and psychedelic policy environments. Survey weights were applied to generate nationally representative estimates.Cannabis was the most commonly microdosed substance (9.4%; 95% CI=8.0, 10.7; 24.1 million adults), followed by psilocybin (5.3%; 95% CI=4.3, 6.3; 13.7 million adults), LSD (4.8%; 95% CI=3.8, 5.9; 12.4 million adults), and MDMA (2.2%; 95% CI=1.5, 2.9; 5.7 million adults). Cannabis (41.2%; 95% CI=33.3, 49.5) was primarily microdosed for medical purposes (e.g., "to manage pain"), while psilocybin (66.6%; 95% CI=56.9, 75.1), LSD (59.2%; 95% CI=46.5, 70.8) and MDMA (86.0%; 95% CI=68.8, 94.5) were more commonly microdosed for recreational purposes (e.g., "to get less high"). articles.title: Microdosing psychedelics: What, why, when, and how often? Insights from an international survey of people who use psychedelics
articles.abstract: The interest in microdosing psychedelics continues to grow within academic and recreational contexts. However, microdosing practices have changed over time, and warrants examination of use patterns within a large, global sample of consumers.The Global Psychedelic Survey 2025 (GPS 2025) was an online, anonymous, cross-sectional survey conducted from May 1-23, 2025. The survey was available in 19 languages and inquired about a wide range of topics surrounding psychedelic use. This manuscript focuses on the primary outcomes for the microdosing component of the survey, examining the substances consumed, dosing regimens employed, reasons for use, as well as the typical 'set and setting' while microdosing.In this sample, 5399 participants reported microdosing during their lifetime, of whom 69.8% (n = 3768) used a microdose within the past year. Psilocybin was the most commonly microdosed substance (n = 4377; 81.1%, 95% CI: 80.0%-82.1%), followed by LSD (n = 2136; 39.6%, 95% CI: 38.3%-40.9%). This was consistent across global regions. The 'Fadiman protocol' (i.e. one day on, two days off) was the most reported dosing regimen among regular microdosers (n = 1203; 24.3%, 95% CI: 23.1%-25.6%). While microdosing, respondents reported often spending time in nature (n = 3087; 58.9%), focusing inwards (n = 2977; 56.8%), or spending leisure time (n = 2253; 43%), demonstrating preliminary evidence supporting the integration of set and setting in the context of microdosing.This study provides

articles.title: Blinding integrity in psychedelic research: Evidence from a comparative randomized controlled trial of psilocybin, MDMA, and methylphenidate in healthy volunteers
articles.abstract: Maintaining effective blinding is a major methodological challenge in psychedelic research. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of blinding integrity in 120 healthy volunteers who received either psilocybin, MDMA, or methylphenidate (active placebo) in a double-blind, randomized controlled trial. Using a multi-level assessment incorporating forced-choice substance guesses, certainty ratings, decision factors, and subjective substance effects, the analyses characterize blinding integrity and its relation to the substance experience. Results indicate that overall blinding was insufficient, with psilocybin showing the highest rates of functional unblinding, MDMA moderate levels, and methylphenidate the lowest. As an active placebo, methylphenidate provided more effective blinding for MDMA than for psilocybin. Incorporating certainty levels of substance guesses revealed a more differentiated pattern, with lower functional unblinding rates. Decision factors and subjective substance experiences were associated with phenomenological substance effects. Prior substance experiences did not influence accuracy of forced-choice substance guesses. These findings provide empirical guidance for the design and reporting of blinding procedures in psychedelic trials and underscore the value of systematic, multi-level assessment of blinding integrity.

articles.title: Considerations for Scaling Psychedelics: Context, Reimbursement, and the Role of the Pharmacy Benefit Manager
articles.abstract: Psychedelic therapies have shown considerable promise in clinical trials, but their effects depend heavily on context—set, setting, therapeutic relationship, and integration—in ways that sit uneasily with health care systems built to finance discrete drugs and billable services. This white paper examines the institutional pathway through which psychedelic therapies may reach patients, from regulatory approval to clinical delivery, payment, and practical access. It reviews the emerging cost-effectiveness literature and identifies three challenges for coverage: valuation (what counts as benefit), duration (the Durability–Churn and Durability–Revenue dilemmas), and delivery (labor intensity and delivery design). It describes a Context–Reimbursement Paradox: the more central context is to therapeutic effect, the harder the intervention is to translate into units that existing payment systems recognize. It then analyzes where pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) fit along a gradient of compatibility, from SSRIs to psilocybin therapy, and argues that drug pricing decisions will shape their role. It closes by considering Indigenous knowledge systems and non-medical pathways to access.

articles.title: Psilocybin and Contrasting Musical Compositions: Effects on Music-Evoked Emotional Responses in Healthy Adults
articles.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>                 <jats:p>Music is a central component of psychedelic settings, yet little experimental work has examined how psilocybin and musical composition influence music-evoked emotional responses in healthy volunteers. This exploratory, double-blind, placebo-controlled study assessed these effects during the plateau phase of psilocybin and the corresponding time window in placebo sessions following oral administration of psilocybin (0.26 mg/kg) or placebo. The study consisted of two parts. In Part 1 (n = 19), a pilot stage, the first half of participants rated music-induced affective valence for eight compositions representing different genres/subgenres (Rock/Punk, Metal/Industrial Metal, Metal/Industrial Metal, Classical/Baroque, Electronic/Dub, Folk/Nordic Folk, Electronic/Techno, Electronic/Trance, Electronic/Psytrance) using a visual analogue scale (VAS). Based on Part 1, the classical composition with the highest overall affective valence and the psytrance composition with the largest psilocybin–placebo contrast (i.e., the composition most responsive to psilocybin) were selected for Part 2 (n = 17), in which the second half of participants assessed emotional responses to music using the Geneva Emotional Music Scale (GEMS-9). Psilocybin increased wonder, transcendence, and joyful activation across both contrasting compositions. Relative to each other, the classical composition elicited greater peacefulness, tenderness, and nostalgia

articles.title: Acute psilocybin or ethocybin leads to a sustained increase in Pavlovian aversion memory in male mice
articles.abstract: <jats:p>There is considerable interest in the concept that psychedelic compounds might facilitate reorganization of emotional processing with therapeutic benefit; in particular, amelioration of excessive focus on past, current and potential-future aversive events, a dominant emotional-cognitive state in stress-related affective disorders. Translational animal models can advance understanding of specific aspects of this concept, namely, those relating to subconscious emotional memories and their neurobiology. In male mice, chronic social stress (CSS) leads to excessive tone/context-foot shock Pavlovian aversion learning (PAL) and memory (PAM), measured as time spent in freezing behavior, and provides a model for generalized excessive focus on aversion. Sub-chronic administration of SSRI antidepressant between PAL and PAM reverses the excessive PAM of CSS mice. Here we applied the model to investigate acute and sustained behavioral and neurobiological effects of psilocybin (PSY) and ethocybin (ETH). In control male mice, both psychedelics at 3 mg/kg per os resulted in 1–2 h of blood-brain exposure to the respective major metabolites psilocin and ethocin, and to head twitch responses. In the main experiment, mice underwent either 15-day CSS or control handling (CON), followed 2 days later by PAL, 1 day later by PSY, ETH or vehicle (VEH), and 3 days later by PAM testing and then brain collection. articles.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF PSILOCYBIN IN TREATMENT-RESISTANT DEPRESSION: A REVIEW
articles.abstract: <jats:p>Major depressive disorder (MDD) is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. A substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve remission through standard monoaminergic therapies, meeting the clinical criteria for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). TRD is associated with significant clinical morbidity and a profound economic burden on healthcare systems. This review evaluates the clinical efficacy, safety profile, and neurobiological mechanisms of psilocybin, a serotonergic psychedelic, as a targeted intervention for TRD. Current neurobiological evidence indicates that psilocybin, upon conversion to its active metabolite psilocin, acts primarily as a 5-HT2A receptor agonist. This mechanism promotes rapid structural neuroplasticity and modulates the aberrant functional connectivity characteristic of severe depression. Recent randomized clinical trials demonstrate that psilocybin, when administered in controlled settings with psychological support, produces rapid and clinically significant reductions in depressive symptoms. Comparative data indicate that its therapeutic efficacy is at least comparable to standard first-line treatments, such as SSRIs, while frequently offering a faster onset of action. Regarding safety, psilocybin is generally well-tolerated in clinical environments; adverse events are typically mild to moderate and transient. However, the strict requirement for concurrent psychological support and rigorous psychiatric screening highlights

articles.title: Development and Psychometric Validation of the ‘Psychedelic Flourishing Scale’
articles.abstract: Positive psychological changes following psychedelic experiences are widely studied, yet no validated instrument has been developed specifically to assess the breadth of enduring change that individuals attribute to those experiences. We therefore conducted a two-part programme of research to evaluate an existing measure and to develop and validate a more comprehensive scale. In Part 1, a preliminary psychometric analysis of the 11-item Mindset Questionnaire (MQ) was conducted using data from two psilocybin studies (N = 97). Its items were strongly intercorrelated (mean inter-item r = .63) and predominantly reflected a single, relatively narrow dimension of change. Part 2 followed established scale-development procedures to define the broader construct of psychedelic flourishing and develop the Psychedelic Flourishing Scale (PFS). A three-round Delphi study involving 17 experts established the construct definition and generated a 41-item pool. The PFS was then evaluated in a pre-registered cross-sectional survey of 1,296 adults who reported previous serotonergic (“classic”) psychedelic use. The sample was randomly divided for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, with the structure extracted in the exploratory half rather than specified in advance. In the confirmatory subsample, a model comprising five correlated facets showed good fit (RMSEA = .053, CFI = .965) and fitted better than a unidimensional model, although a four-factor model performed similarly.
